# -within keeps only edges whose caller and callee are both in the package,
# including methods, whose names embed the package path in parentheses.
calltree -within=example.com/m -trim=example.com/m. -f graph.txt
cmp stdout want.txt

# -edges writes the filtered graph back in the input format, quoting any name
# holding a space so that digraph can read it again.
calltree -within=example.com/m -trim=example.com/m. -edges -tag=prod -f graph.txt
cmp stdout want-edges.txt

# An empty result after -within is an error: it means the graph loaded partially.
! calltree -within=example.com/nothing -f graph.txt
stderr 'no edge has both ends'

# A root that is not in the graph is an error, not an empty tree.
! calltree -within=example.com/m -trim=example.com/m. -f graph.txt nosuch
stderr 'no node named "nosuch"'

-- graph.txt --
example.com/m.main	example.com/m.run
example.com/m.main	fmt.Println
runtime.main	example.com/m.main
example.com/m.run	(*example.com/m.T).M
example.com/m.run	example.com/m.New[func(i int) error]
-- want.txt --
main
  -> run
    -> (*T).M
    -> New[func(i int) error]
-- want-edges.txt --
prod: main run
prod: run (*T).M
prod: run "New[func(i int) error]"
